name: A leaf, a flower, offered with love
meaning: Whatever is offered with devotion, even a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, is accepted; it is the love that matters, not the size.
applies_when: Someone feels their contribution, practice or gift is too small to matter.
misleads_when: It is used to excuse never doing more when more is possible.
modern_application: Make one small, sincere offering today: a call, a meal, a minute of attention.

name: Take refuge with your whole being
meaning: Take refuge in the Lord with your whole being, and you will reach supreme peace; those who take refuge cross the confusion of the world.
applies_when: Someone feels alone and overwhelmed, and draws strength from faith.
misleads_when: It is used to discourage seeking practical, medical or professional help.
modern_application: Alongside prayer or reflection, name one practical support you will also reach out to.

name: Keep the highest in mind
meaning: For one who remembers God constantly, with a mind that turns to nothing else, God is easy to reach; fix the mind there and you will come there.
applies_when: Someone wants a steady centre amid a busy life.
misleads_when: It is used to neglect present duties or relationships.
modern_application: Choose a word, verse or image that reminds you of what is highest for you, and return to it at three set moments each day.

name: If you can't do the highest, do the next
meaning: If you cannot fix your mind steadily, practise; if you cannot practise, work for God; if you cannot even do that, give up the fruit of your actions. There is always a next step.
applies_when: Someone feels they are failing at their ideal and are tempted to give up entirely.
misleads_when: It is used to settle for less when someone could do more.
modern_application: If your ideal routine is too much, drop to the level you can actually keep, and do that faithfully.

name: Letting go of the fruit brings peace
meaning: Giving up the fruit of action is ranked even above meditation: peace follows at once from it; the disciplined who give up the fruit find lasting peace.
applies_when: Someone cannot find peace because they are fixated on a specific outcome.
misleads_when: It is used to stop someone advocating for a fair result.
modern_application: Write the outcome you are holding on to, then write: 'I will do my part, and I will be all right either way.'

name: A purpose beyond pleasure
meaning: Having glimpsed the ageless, who would delight in a long life of fading pleasures? The good leads beyond the merely pleasant.
applies_when: Someone has comfort but feels their life lacks meaning.
misleads_when: It is used to dismiss legitimate enjoyment of life.
modern_application: Write one sentence about what you would want your life to have served, beyond your own comfort.

name: The light by which everything shines
meaning: There the sun does not shine, nor moon or stars; everything shines after that light, and by its light all this is lit. It dwells in every heart.
applies_when: Someone feels in the dark and needs a sense that something within them does not go out.
misleads_when: It is used to dismiss depression as a lack of inner light.
modern_application: Sit in a dark room for two minutes with a single candle or lamp, and reflect that awareness itself is what lets you see anything.

name: The divine is the friend of all
meaning: Knowing God as the friend of all beings brings peace; God is the goal, support, refuge and friend.
applies_when: Someone feels abandoned or unloved.
misleads_when: It replaces human connection and support entirely.
modern_application: Let yourself be befriended today: accept one kindness offered to you without deflecting it.

name: See the sacred in excellence
meaning: Whatever is glorious, prosperous or powerful springs from a spark of the divine splendour.
applies_when: Someone wants to connect their pursuit of excellence or beauty with something larger.
misleads_when: It is used to worship power or success as such.
modern_application: When you see something excellent, whether a skill, a kindness or a view, pause to appreciate where it comes from.

name: Intention and faith give an act its worth
meaning: An act done because it ought to be done, without seeking reward, is pure; whatever is done without faith is of no use here or hereafter.
applies_when: Someone is going through the motions of a duty or practice without meaning it.
misleads_when: It is used to discourage doing good while one's motives are still mixed.
modern_application: Before a routine duty, pause and name honestly why you are doing it. Adjust the 'why' if you can.

name: When duties conflict, name the confusion
meaning: Arjuna's duties to family, teachers and his role collide; he says plainly that his mind is confused about what is right and asks for one clear answer. The Gita begins from that honesty.
applies_when: Two obligations genuinely conflict: career versus family, loyalty versus honesty, parent versus partner.
misleads_when: It is used to look for one authority to decide everything.
modern_application: Write each duty and to whom it is owed. Ask which can be partly met, which can wait, and which cannot be compromised.

name: Renounce selfish intent, not your responsibilities
meaning: A true renunciant is one who does what should be done without depending on its fruit, who neither hates nor craves; what they call renunciation is giving up selfish intentions.
applies_when: Someone thinks spiritual growth means walking away from family, study or work.
misleads_when: It is used to keep someone in a harmful or dangerous situation. Leaving abuse or danger is never 'selfish'.
modern_application: Keep your commitments, and look for the selfish intention inside them that you could let go of instead.

name: The path of withdrawal and solitude
meaning: For some, the highest perfection comes through renunciation: solitude, light eating, controlled speech, dispassion, and giving up possessions and the sense of 'mine'.
applies_when: An adult, usually in later life, with responsibilities fulfilled or handed over, is considering a life of retreat or full-time spiritual practice.
misleads_when: It is presented to someone in distress, to anyone under 18, or to someone escaping responsibilities or problems. Never recommended to them.
modern_application: Try retreat in measured steps (a weekend, then a week) while keeping your obligations covered, and discuss it with those who depend on you.

name: Renunciation and engaged action both lead to the good, but action is easier
meaning: Renunciation and the yoga of action both lead to the highest good, but of the two the yoga of action is better; renunciation is hard to reach without it.
applies_when: Someone is choosing between a contemplative and an active life.
misleads_when: It is used to dismiss genuinely contemplative vocations.
modern_application: Start by bringing contemplation into your active life (daily practice, service) before deciding on any larger change.

name: Hold action and contemplation together
meaning: The Isha warns against pursuing either ignorance or knowledge alone; whoever knows both together crosses death by one and reaches immortality by the other.
applies_when: Someone has swung to one extreme: all work and no reflection, or all study and no engagement.
misleads_when: It is used to avoid ever committing fully to anything.
modern_application: Put one reflective practice into a busy week, or one practical commitment into a reflective life.

name: Your nature shapes what you do
meaning: Beings follow their nature, and no being is free of the three qualities; one's nature and faith shape what one becomes.
applies_when: Someone is fighting their temperament in choosing a career or way of life, and needs to work with it.
misleads_when: It turns into fatalism ('I can't change'), or excuses harm. Never offered as fatalism to anyone in distress or under 18.
modern_application: List what reliably energises you and what reliably drains you. Shape your next choice around the first list.

name: A larger power moves all beings
meaning: The Lord dwells in every heart, moving all beings as if on a machine; what you refuse out of confusion, your nature will make you do.
applies_when: An adult wants to let go of excessive control and see their life in a larger frame.
misleads_when: It is used as fatalism, to deny responsibility, or with anyone in distress or under 18. The surrounding verses also concern going to war. Restricted.
modern_application: Notice where you are trying to control what you cannot. Hold your part firmly and the rest more loosely.

name: Keep your word, as good people always have
meaning: Nachiketas urges his father to keep his word: look at how those before acted and how good people act now; no one becomes ageless by breaking it.
applies_when: An adult is tempted to break a serious promise for convenience.
misleads_when: It is used to hold someone to a promise that would cause harm, or one made under pressure. The original story involves a child sent to Death; restricted for under-18s and anyone in distress.
modern_application: Before breaking a promise, tell the person directly and offer what you can instead.

name: Dharma includes protecting the good
meaning: Whenever dharma declines, the divine acts to protect the good and restore order; righteousness is not passive.
applies_when: Someone is deciding whether to speak up or act against injustice they witness.
misleads_when: It is used to justify violence or vigilantism. Viveka applies it only to lawful, non-violent protection and reporting.
modern_application: If you witness harm, take the safest effective step: support the person, document it, and report it to someone with authority.

name: Steady understanding under pressure
meaning: One of steady wisdom is not shaken by sorrow, does not crave pleasure, and is free of passion, fear and anger; such a mind does not waver.
applies_when: Someone faces a high-pressure situation (an exam, a negotiation, a crisis at work or home) and needs to stay clear.
misleads_when: It is used to suppress the body's legitimate stress signals.
modern_application: Prepare for the pressure moment: rehearse it once, plan your first sentence, and decide in advance how you will steady yourself.

name: When clarity returns, act on it
meaning: At the end, Arjuna says: my delusion is gone, my doubts resolved, I stand firm and will act. Clarity is meant to end in a decision.
applies_when: Someone has reached clarity but keeps postponing the decision.
misleads_when: It is used to rush a decision before clarity has really come.
modern_application: If you know what you need to do, set a date this week to take the first step, and tell one person.
